case: Adult, age 48; GBM IDH-wildtype methylation class RTK II; 1.2 cm lesion gross-totally resected 2 weeks ago; treatment-naive; MGMT-unmethylated-requiring trials excluded from this list per case direction
scope: US; recruiting or not-yet-recruiting; adult; immunotherapy or EGFR-targeted; open to newly diagnosed disease; excludes trials requiring MGMT-unmethylated status for this case

trials.name: DOC1021 (dubodencel) dendritic-cell vaccine + standard care
trials.biomarker_needed: IDH-wildtype required; MGMT / EGFR not restricted
trials.tissue_requirement: Fresh (viable) tumour specimen required at surgery — not just a paraffin block. Confirm what was preserved from the 1.2 cm resection.
trials.postop_timing: No explicit day-count stated; the general rule for this window is to enrol before chemoradiation starts (typically ~4–6 weeks post-op). At 2 weeks post-op, this window is open now but time-limited.
trials.us_sites: CA (City of Hope, HOAG, UCSF), FL (Baptist MD Anderson Jacksonville), MA (Dana-Farber), NJ (Cooper, Rutgers, Atlantic), NY (Lenox Hill), NC (UNC, Wake Forest), OH (Ohio State), PA (UPMC), TN (Vanderbilt), TX (UTHealth, Baylor, UT San Antonio)
trials.timing: Enrol after resection, before starting radiation/temozolomide (leukapheresis + tumour specimen needed).
trials.why_this_fit: Built for exactly this scenario — newly diagnosed, IDH-wildtype, near-complete resection, no prior therapy. Randomised, many US sites. Needs a fresh tumour specimen from the resection: confirm tissue was banked.
trials.key_inclusion: Age ≥18; presumed newly diagnosed IDH-wildtype GBM | Gross-total / near-total resection (≥95% of enhancing tumour removed, ≤1 cm³ residual) — ≥70% subtotal also allowed | KPS ≥70 | No prior anti-cancer treatment for GBM | Hb ≥8, ANC ≥1500, platelets ≥75k
trials.key_exclusion: Infratentorial, recurrent, leptomeningeal or extracranial disease | Autoimmune disease needing immunosuppression within 2 years | DMARDs / TNF inhibitors / anti-CD20 / JAK inhibitors | Investigational drug within 30 days
trials.secondary_endpoints: 1-, 2-, 3-year survival; adverse events (CTCAE v5); time to progression (RANO 2.0).
trials.outcomes_so_far: Phase 1 (n=16 newly diagnosed; 94% MGMT-unmethylated, a poor-prognosis group): 1-year overall survival 88% vs 53% in an age-matched control cohort (p<0.002); 93% (14/15 evaluable) alive beyond 12 months; no serious vaccine-attributable adverse events. Supported progression to this randomised phase 2. (ASCO 2025)
trials.evidence_note: Single-arm phase 1 (n=16 newly diagnosed): 1-year OS 88% vs 53% in age-matched controls (p<0.002).
trials.flags: Requires a fresh tumour specimen — verify what was preserved from the 1.2 cm resection.

trials.name: AV-GBM-1 tumour-initiating-cell dendritic-cell vaccine
trials.biomarker_needed: IDH and MGMT status documented (not restricted); EGFR not applicable
trials.tissue_requirement: Needs a viable tumour cell line established from fresh surgical tissue, not archival tissue.
trials.postop_timing: Same before-chemoradiation window as DOC1021 (open now, closes once chemoradiation starts) — but this trial is currently Not yet recruiting, so timing also depends on when it opens.
trials.us_sites: US sites not yet listed on the registry.
trials.timing: Tumour harvested at initial surgery to establish a cell line; leukapheresis; randomise after recovery, before starting radiation/temozolomide.
trials.why_this_fit: Blinded, placebo-controlled phase 3 in exactly this population, with encouraging phase 2 data. Requires a viable tumour cell line grown from surgical tissue — confirm fresh tissue availability. Not yet open; watch for activation.
trials.key_inclusion: Newly diagnosed primary GBM, histologically confirmed | Age >18; KPS ≥70 | Recovered from maximal safe resection with an established tumour cell line | Planning to start radiation + temozolomide
trials.key_exclusion: Prior astrocytoma / glial tumour | Autoimmune disease or immunodeficiency | Other invasive cancer within 5 years | GM-CSF allergy; cardiac disease needing active treatment
trials.secondary_endpoints: PFS and OS from first vaccine dose; PFS from randomisation; treatment-emergent adverse events.
trials.outcomes_so_far: Phase 2 (n=57 who started vaccine): median PFS 10.4 months (vs ~6.9 historical), median OS 16.0 months; 12- and 15-month OS 76%; 2-year OS 27%. Main vaccine-related events were injection-site reactions and flu-like symptoms. (JECCR 2022; 3-yr follow-up 2025)
trials.evidence_note: Phase 2 (n=57): median PFS 10.4 mo and median OS 16.0 mo vs ~6.9 / ~15 mo historical; 2-year OS 27%.
trials.flags: Not yet recruiting. | Needs a viable tumour cell line from surgery — verify fresh tissue was banked.
trials.dates: Listed start Jan 2024 (delayed) · primary completion Mar 2028

trials.name: GBM AGILE adaptive platform trial
trials.biomarker_needed: IDH-wildtype grade 4 GBM; MGMT status guides which arm you can be assigned to
trials.tissue_requirement: No special tissue banking — the standard pathology block from any resection is enough; the assigned arm may add its own biomarker testing.
trials.postop_timing: Open now — must enrol before starting chemoradiation, the same general window as the other pre-chemoradiation vaccine trials.
trials.us_sites: ~30+ US sites incl. UAB, UC San Diego, Cedars-Sinai, St Joseph (Orange, CA), U Colorado, Yale, Sylvester/Miami, MGH, Dana-Farber, Mount Sinai, Columbia, MSK, Cleveland Clinic, UPMC, MD Anderson, Huntsman, UVA.
trials.timing: Newly diagnosed: enrol before starting chemoradiation. Recurrent arms also open.
trials.why_this_fit: The broadest single access route — one screening, randomisation to a novel agent plus a proper control, ~30+ US sites. But the arm you get is assigned, and may not be an immunotherapy or EGFR-targeted agent. Ask which arms are open at the nearby site.
trials.key_inclusion: Age ≥18; histologically confirmed grade 4 GBM, IDH-wildtype | MRI within 21 days; KPS ≥60 (newly diagnosed) / ≥70 (recurrent) | Tumour tissue available | No prior GBM therapy (newly diagnosed cohort)
trials.key_exclusion: Prior carmustine wafer or prior intracerebral agents | Extensive leptomeningeal disease | QTc >470 ms | Second malignancy within 2 years | Early progression <3 months from radiation (recurrent)
trials.secondary_endpoints: Progression-free survival; tumour response; duration of response.
trials.outcomes_so_far: The platform is designed to read arms out efficiently rather than to have one headline result. Some arms have been negative (e.g. regorafenib, JCO 2025). Value here is faster access to novel agents with randomisation against a real control.
trials.evidence_note: A platform: each arm has its own evidence. Some arms have read out negative (e.g. regorafenib). The design itself is validated as an efficient way to test agents against a shared control.
trials.flags: Mechanism is assigned by randomisation — confirm an immunotherapy / targeted arm is enrolling.

trials.name: Bvax — autologous B-cell vaccination + chemoradiation
trials.biomarker_needed: Histologically confirmed GBM; IDH / MGMT / EGFR not specified
trials.tissue_requirement: Needs ≥ 1.5 g of fresh-frozen tumour tissue plus a paraffin block from the resection.
trials.postop_timing: Appears to allow enrolment even after starting first-line chemoradiation, so this window is less tightly time-limited than the others — but not yet recruiting (opens ~Sep 2026).
trials.sponsor: Northwestern University (Catalina Lee-Chang; PI of record Roger Stupp)
trials.timing: Opens ~Sep 2026. Needs ≥1.5 g fresh-frozen tumour tissue + a paraffin block; no prior therapy except surgery ± first-line chemoradiation.
trials.why_this_fit: Mechanistically novel and open to newly diagnosed disease with standard chemoradiation. Two practical limits: a single site, and a requirement for ≥1.5 g of fresh-frozen tumour tissue — unlikely to be available retrospectively after a completed 1.2 cm resection unless it was specifically banked fresh-frozen.
trials.key_inclusion: Histologically confirmed GBM with FFPE block and ≥1.5 g fresh-frozen tissue | Age ≥18; ECOG ≤2 | Adequate organ / marrow function without transfusion support
trials.key_exclusion: Unrecovered surgical / chemoradiation toxicity > grade 2 | Concurrent investigational agents | Allergy to DMSO, CryoStor CS10, or ethylene-vinyl-acetate | Uncontrolled infection or cardiac disease
trials.primary_endpoint: Incidence of adverse events (CTCAE v6), up to 90 days after first dose.
trials.secondary_endpoints: Progression-free and overall survival rate (up to 5 years).
trials.flags: Not yet recruiting; single site. | Needs 1.5 g fresh-frozen tumour tissue — confirm before counting on this.
trials.dates: Estimated start Sep 2026 · primary completion Sep 2028

trials.name: BreakVax personalised vaccine + dual checkpoint + temozolomide
trials.biomarker_needed: Histologically confirmed GBM; IDH / MGMT / EGFR not specified; excludes dMMR/MSI-H and POLE-mutant
trials.tissue_requirement: Needs ~200 mg of tumour tissue from the original resection, AND a new on-treatment biopsy during the trial.
trials.postop_timing: Not tied to a specific post-op week; gated on the trial opening (~Sep 2026) and on-treatment biopsy logistics rather than a surgery-clock deadline.
trials.us_sites: FL — Miami (Herbert Wertheim Cancer Institute / Miami Cancer Institute).
trials.timing: Opens ~Sep 2026. Needs ~200 mg tumour tissue; on-treatment biopsy required.
trials.why_this_fit: Very small (n=10), single site, not yet open, and unusually steroid-restrictive (no systemic steroids within 6 weeks, cannot require steroids). Checkpoint-heavy regimen despite checkpoint monotherapy having failed in newly diagnosed GBM. Worth tracking as it opens.
trials.key_inclusion: Age 18–71; histologically confirmed GBM with 200 mg tissue submitted | KPS ≥80; life expectancy >6 months | No prior anti-PD-1 / PD-L1; no immunosuppression within 12 months
trials.key_exclusion: Any systemic or topical steroids within 6 weeks; cannot require steroid pre-medication | Autoimmune disease (limited exceptions) | Myocarditis / CHF / LVEF <50%; interstitial lung disease | Uncontrolled hypertension; coumarin anticoagulants; strong CYP3A4 modulators | Prior invasive cancer within 2 years; dMMR/MSI-H; POLE mutation
trials.primary_endpoint: Overall survival (12 months); BreakVax manufacturing success; adverse events.
trials.secondary_endpoints: Change in tumour-infiltrating T cells; immune-related ORR / PFS / duration of response (iRANO / RANO); pseudoprogression rate.
trials.flags: Not yet recruiting; single site; n=10. | Strict steroid exclusion — hard to meet if any steroid is needed for oedema.
trials.dates: Estimated start Sep 2026 · primary completion Sep 2030

trials.name: GIANT — perioperative nivolumab ± relatlimab
trials.biomarker_needed: Newly diagnosed IDH-wildtype; MGMT status determined (guides temozolomide); no EGFR requirement
trials.tissue_requirement: Requires an upcoming, not-yet-completed tumour resection — dosed before surgery. Not applicable after a completed resection unless disease recurs.
trials.postop_timing: Not applicable — requires a resection that has not happened yet. The resection 2 weeks ago already closed this door unless disease recurs.
trials.us_sites: NC — Duke; NY — Memorial Sloan Kettering. (Also Peter MacCallum, Australia.)
trials.timing: Requires an upcoming resection — enrol before the definitive tumour surgery.
trials.why_this_fit: The design needs a planned biopsy → drug → definitive resection. This patient's 1.2 cm lesion has already had a gross-total resection, so there is likely no tumour left to enrol against. Relevant only if the MRI shows residual/measurable disease, or at recurrence.
trials.key_inclusion: Newly diagnosed IDH-wildtype GBM, deemed resectable (gross-total resection feasible) | Age ≥18; ECOG 0–1; life expectancy ≥12 months | Steroids ≤2 mg/day dexamethasone-equivalent | No prior immunosuppressive therapy or active autoimmune disease
trials.key_exclusion: Gross-total resection not feasible; cerebellar / brainstem / deep basal-ganglia tumour | Urgent resection needed (mass effect, hydrocephalus) | CNS bleed or stroke within 6 months | Active autoimmune disease; myocarditis history; SARS-CoV-2 within 4 weeks
trials.primary_endpoint: Safety-lead-in toxicity; feasibility (biopsy → neoadjuvant → surgery); change in tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes from biopsy to resection.
trials.secondary_endpoints: Overall and progression-free survival; RANO response; perioperative morbidity; pharmacokinetics.
trials.outcomes_so_far: No GIANT data yet. Context: checkpoint monotherapy was negative in newly diagnosed GBM (CheckMate-498: nivolumab + radiation median OS 13.4 vs 14.9 months for temozolomide + radiation; CheckMate-548: no benefit). Neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 produced immune activation and a survival signal in a small randomised recurrent-GBM study (Cloughesy, 2019). Dual PD-1/LAG-3 blockade and the perioperative schedule are the new elements. (review)
trials.evidence_note: GIANT has not reported. Checkpoint-inhibitor monotherapy was negative in newly diagnosed GBM (CheckMate-498, CheckMate-548); neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 gave an immune and survival signal in a small recurrent-GBM randomised study. Dual PD-1/LAG-3 + the perioperative schedule are the untested elements.
trials.flags: Needs tumour still in place for a planned resection — not applicable after a completed gross-total resection unless disease recurs.

trials.name: Carmustine wafer + retifanlimab (anti-PD-1) + radiation ± temozolomide
trials.biomarker_needed: Newly diagnosed grade 4 GBM / gliosarcoma; MGMT / IDH / EGFR not specified
trials.tissue_requirement: Wafers are placed directly in the resection cavity at surgery — requires a not-yet-completed resection.
trials.postop_timing: Not applicable — wafers had to be placed at the original surgery.
trials.timing: Carmustine wafers placed at resection — must enrol before / at the tumour surgery; post-op imaging within 72 hours.
trials.why_this_fit: Entry requires carmustine wafers to be placed at the tumour resection. That resection is already done here (without wafers), so this would need a future surgery. Listed for completeness.
trials.key_inclusion: Newly diagnosed grade 4 GBM / gliosarcoma with carmustine wafers placed at resection | No prior GBM treatment except surgery + wafer | Age ≥18; KPS ≥60; appropriate for concurrent temozolomide + radiation
trials.key_exclusion: Recurrent GBM | CNS haemorrhage > grade 1 on baseline MRI | Prior anti-PD-1 / PD-L1 / CTLA-4 | Active autoimmune disease; live vaccine within 28 days; probiotic supplements
trials.primary_endpoint: Safety, feasibility, maximum tolerated dose (up to 2 years).
trials.secondary_endpoints: Progression-free survival; overall response rate; overall survival by MGMT status.
trials.evidence_note: No results posted. Randomised pilot; carmustine wafers + anti-PD-1.
trials.flags: Requires wafers placed at the resection — not compatible with a resection already completed without them.

trials.name: BRiTE — EGFRvIII×CD3 bispecific T-cell engager
trials.biomarker_needed: EGFRvIII mutation required; supratentorial grade 4 GBM
trials.tissue_requirement: Off-the-shelf antibody infusion — no cell manufacturing; EGFRvIII status uses the existing archival block.
trials.postop_timing: Gated on radiation, not surgery directly — enrol ≥4 weeks after finishing radiation. Since radiation has not started yet, this trial is not reachable for roughly another 3–4 months from today.
trials.sponsor: Duke University (Mustafa Khasraw; with Adaptin Bio)
trials.timing: After resection + standard radiation (± temozolomide by MGMT). MGMT-unmethylated: radiation alone, enrol ≥4 weeks after radiation. Enhancing disease ≤4 cm before resection.
trials.why_this_fit: A fit only if EGFRvIII-positive. Single site, small early-phase study. Antigen escape (loss of EGFRvIII under pressure) has limited previous EGFRvIII-directed therapies — the secreted-engager design is meant to address that.
trials.key_inclusion: Age ≥18; supratentorial grade 4 GBM with confirmed EGFRvIII | KPS ≥70; Hb ≥9, ANC ≥750, platelets ≥50k | Steroids <2 mg/day dexamethasone within 7 days | Newly diagnosed: only surgery + standard radiation/temozolomide beforehand
trials.key_exclusion: QTc >480 ms; impending herniation | Prior unrelated malignancy (few exceptions) | Active infection; HIV with CD4 <350; uncontrolled hepatitis | NYHA 3–4 heart disease; autoimmune disease within 3 months | Newly diagnosed with biopsy only (no resection)
trials.outcomes_so_far: No BRiTE efficacy data reported yet. Earlier EGFRvIII-directed approaches at Duke (an EGFRvIII bispecific and EGFRvIII CAR-T) showed antigen loss and limited durable benefit — the central challenge this design targets.
trials.evidence_note: No BRiTE efficacy data reported. Earlier EGFRvIII-directed therapies at this centre were limited by antigen escape — the design this trial tests.
trials.flags: Requires EGFRvIII-positive. Single site; small phase 1.

trials.name: WSD0922-FU ± adjuvant temozolomide, randomised
trials.biomarker_needed: Newly diagnosed GBM, IDH-wildtype, PATHOGENIC EGFR MUTATION (± amplification) by CLIA NGS — includes EGFRvIII and point mutations. EGFR amplification ALONE does not qualify. MGMT status must be known.
trials.tissue_requirement: Standard archival tissue for EGFR mutation/EGFRvIII testing — no special banking needed.
trials.postop_timing: Gated on radiation — register ≥2 weeks after radiation and ≥3 weeks after surgery. The 3-weeks-post-surgery part will be satisfied soon; the real gate is finishing radiation first.
trials.us_sites: MN — Mayo Clinic, Rochester (recruiting). AZ (Scottsdale) and FL (Jacksonville) sites pending.
trials.timing: After standard 60 Gy + concurrent temozolomide, before adjuvant temozolomide; register ≥2 weeks after radiation and ≥3 weeks after surgery.
trials.why_this_fit: A strong fit if the NGS report shows a pathogenic EGFR mutation or EGFRvIII. Important nuance for RTK II: many of these tumours are EGFR-amplified without a point mutation, and amplification-only tumours are explicitly excluded here — check the exact finding.
trials.key_inclusion: Newly diagnosed GBM, IDH-wildtype (WHO 2021) | Pathogenic EGFR mutation ± amplification by CLIA NGS (point mutations or EGFRvIII) | MGMT methylation testing done | ECOG 0–2; Hb >9, ANC >1.5k, platelets >100k, CrCl ≥45
trials.key_exclusion: EGFR wild-type; amplification alone without a pathogenic mutation; variants of unknown significance | True progression outside the radiation field | Prior adjuvant temozolomide, EGFR inhibitor, chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or bevacizumab | Active keratitis; significant cardiac disease; other active malignancy within 3 years
trials.secondary_endpoints: Adverse events; overall survival; overall response rate.
trials.outcomes_so_far: WSD0922-FU is in early-phase testing as a CNS-penetrant EGFR inhibitor; no randomised efficacy data yet.
trials.evidence_note: WSD0922-FU is in early testing as a CNS-penetrant EGFR inhibitor; no efficacy readout yet.
trials.flags: Requires a pathogenic EGFR mutation / EGFRvIII — EGFR amplification alone is excluded.

trials.name: ABBV-637 or ABBV-155 + ERAS-801 (EGFR ADC + EGFR TKI)
trials.biomarker_needed: Grade 4 GBM / gliosarcoma, IDH-wildtype, EGFR GENE AMPLIFICATION required (CLIA assay)
trials.tissue_requirement: Standard archival tissue for EGFR amplification testing — no special banking needed.
trials.postop_timing: Starts alongside chemoradiation, so it becomes reachable once radiation begins (typically ~4–6 weeks post-op) — not immediately actionable at 2 weeks post-op.
trials.us_sites: NY (MSK Manhattan + Westchester + regional sites), NJ (MSK Basking Ridge / Monmouth / Bergen), CA (UCLA), FL (University of Miami), IN (Indiana University), VT (University of Vermont).
trials.timing: Newly-diagnosed cohorts C/D: drug given with radiation + temozolomide (standard timing).
trials.why_this_fit: One of the few newly-diagnosed trials that enrols on EGFR amplification alone — the classic RTK II lesion — so potentially a High fit if the tumour is amplified. Caveats: early-phase (dose-finding, toxicity-focused), and the prior EGFR antibody-drug conjugate depatuxizumab-mafodotin failed to improve survival in this exact population.
trials.key_inclusion: Grade 4 GBM / gliosarcoma, IDH-wildtype | EGFR gene amplification by CLIA assay | Age ≥18; KPS ≥60; LVEF ≥50%, QTc <450 ms | Paraffin tissue from the initial resection available
trials.key_exclusion: Prior EGFR-targeted therapy | Enzyme-inducing anti-epileptic drugs within 10 days | Significant cardiac disease / arrhythmia / pericardial disease within 6 months | Active hepatitis; strong CYP3A modulators; live vaccine within 2 weeks
trials.outcomes_so_far: No results yet (phase 1b). Cautionary precedent: the EGFR antibody-drug conjugate depatuxizumab-mafodotin did not improve overall survival in EGFR-amplified newly diagnosed GBM (INTELLANCE-1, randomised phase 3).
trials.evidence_note: No results yet. The prior EGFR antibody-drug conjugate depatuxizumab-mafodotin did NOT improve overall survival in EGFR-amplified newly diagnosed GBM in the randomised phase 3 INTELLANCE-1.
trials.flags: Requires EGFR amplification. | Early-phase, dose-finding — primary endpoint is toxicity, not efficacy.

trials.name: ERAS-801 EGFR inhibitor (ERAS-801-SARG)
trials.biomarker_needed: IDH-wildtype with EGFR amplification and/or mutation (excludes T790M, exon 20). Newly-diagnosed cohort C is restricted to age ≥70.
trials.tissue_requirement: Standard archival tissue for EGFR-alteration testing — no special banking needed.
trials.postop_timing: Cohort C’s stated window is 2–4 weeks after surgery — at exactly 2 weeks post-op today, this window is open now and closes soon. However, Cohort C is restricted to age ≥70, which rules it out for a 48-year-old regardless of timing.
trials.sponsor: UCLA Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center (with NCI)
trials.us_sites: CA — UCLA (recruiting). NY — Memorial Sloan Kettering (not yet).
trials.timing: Cohort C: enrol 2–4 weeks after surgery.
trials.why_this_fit: The newly-diagnosed cohort is elderly-only (age ≥70). For a younger adult it is relevant only at recurrence, via the surgical-window cohorts.
trials.key_inclusion: Cohort C: age ≥70; newly diagnosed grade 4 GBM / gliosarcoma, IDH-wildtype, with EGFR amplification and/or mutation | KPS ≥60; craniotomy site healed | LVEF normal; QTcF ≤450 ms; ANC ≥1000, platelets ≥100k, Hb ≥9
trials.key_exclusion: Prior EGFR inhibitor | Enzyme-inducing anti-epileptic drugs | Significant intracranial haemorrhage | MI / unstable angina within 6 months; QTcF >450 ms; uncontrolled hypertension | CYP3A4 / 2C8 / 2D6 modulators
trials.primary_endpoint: Cohort C: 6-month progression-free survival. Cohort A: FDG-PET SUV change. Cohort B: pharmacokinetics / QTc.
trials.secondary_endpoints: Adverse events; glycolytic index (FDG-PET / pH-weighted MRI); pharmacokinetics; response.
trials.outcomes_so_far: ERAS-801 in a small phase 1 recurrent EGFR-altered cohort: progression-free survival ≥6 months and one partial response among 6 patients, with favourable CNS exposure and tolerability.
trials.evidence_note: ERAS-801 phase 1 (recurrent EGFR-altered GBM): PFS ≥6 months and one partial response among 6 patients, with favourable CNS exposure.

trials.name: BDTX-1535 (silevertinib) Phase 0/1 surgical-window study
trials.biomarker_needed: EGFR alterations — variants, fusions, mutations, ± amplification. Newly-diagnosed arms stratified by MGMT.
trials.tissue_requirement: Requires a scheduled resection to measure drug levels directly in tumour tissue — not applicable after a completed resection.
trials.postop_timing: Not applicable — needs a still-scheduled resection to measure drug levels in the tumour.
trials.sponsor: Ivy Brain Tumor Center / St Joseph's Hospital, Phoenix (Barrow Neurological Institute)
trials.us_sites: AZ — Ivy Brain Tumor Center (Chandler and Phoenix).
trials.timing: Requires a scheduled resection with measurable enhancing disease ≥1 cm.
trials.why_this_fit: A surgical-window design that needs measurable enhancing tumour and a scheduled resection — not applicable after a completed gross-total resection unless disease recurs. Arizona only. (The randomised newly-diagnosed silevertinib trial, NCT07326566, would otherwise have been a better fit but required MGMT-unmethylated status and was removed from this list.)
trials.key_inclusion: EGFR alteration (variant, fusion, mutation ± amplification) | Newly diagnosed grade 4 GBM (arms C–E) or recurrent high-grade glioma (arms A–B) | Candidate for clinical resection with measurable pre-operative disease | Age ≥18; ECOG ≤2; steroids stable / decreasing ≥5 days
trials.key_exclusion: Leptomeningeal disease; interstitial lung disease | Severe GI disease / baseline ≥ grade 2 diarrhoea | Significant cardiovascular disease | Strong CYP2C8 / CYP3A4 modulators
trials.primary_endpoint: Unbound and total BDTX-1535 concentration in tumour tissue; dose-limiting toxicities.
trials.secondary_endpoints: CSF drug levels; change in phospho-EGFR / phospho-ERK; 6-month PFS; median PFS / OS.
trials.outcomes_so_far: BDTX-1535 phase 1 (recurrent high-grade glioma with EGFR alterations) showed CNS penetration and early activity at 200 mg; this study measures target engagement directly in resected tissue.
trials.evidence_note: BDTX-1535 phase 1 showed brain-tumour drug exposure and early activity at 200 mg; this Phase 0/1 measures target engagement directly in resected tissue.
trials.flags: Needs tumour still in place for a planned resection — not applicable now.

trials.name: Super-selective intra-arterial cetuximab + blood-brain-barrier disruption
trials.biomarker_needed: Pathology-confirmed EGFR overexpression required; IDH / MGMT not specified
trials.tissue_requirement: Standard archival tissue for EGFR overexpression testing — no special banking needed.
trials.postop_timing: Flexible — timed around standard care rather than a fixed post-op deadline (needs 2+ weeks clear of chemo and 8+ weeks clear of radiation around each procedure).
trials.us_sites: NY — Lenox Hill Hospital / Brain Tumor Center, New York City.
trials.timing: No chemotherapy within 2 weeks and no external-beam radiation within 8 weeks of each procedure — fits around standard care.
trials.why_this_fit: Relevant if the tumour is EGFR-overexpressing / amplified. Single site; long-running with slow accrual (open since 2016). Systemic cetuximab has not worked in GBM, so intra-arterial delivery past the blood-brain barrier is the specific hypothesis.
trials.key_inclusion: Newly diagnosed GBM, biopsy-proven | Pathology-confirmed EGFR overexpression | Age ≥18; KPS ≥70 or ECOG 0–2; expected survival ≥3 months | Adequate counts and organ function
trials.key_exclusion: Leptomeningeal disease | Cetuximab allergy | Significant intercurrent medical or psychiatric illness
trials.outcomes_so_far: The Northwell group has reported that intra-arterial cetuximab with blood-brain-barrier disruption is feasible and generally safe, with occasional radiographic responses in EGFR-overexpressing GBM. No controlled efficacy data.
trials.evidence_note: The Northwell group reports intra-arterial cetuximab with blood-brain-barrier disruption is feasible and generally safe, with occasional radiographic responses in EGFR-overexpressing GBM. No controlled efficacy data. Systemic cetuximab has not worked in GBM.
trials.flags: Requires EGFR overexpression. Single site; slow historical accrual.

trials.name: DB107-RRV retroviral vector + 5-fluorocytosine + radiation
trials.biomarker_needed: Newly diagnosed adult-type diffuse glioma; IDH1 and MGMT testing required; tumour ≤5 cm; candidate for ≥80% resection of enhancing tumour
trials.tissue_requirement: Vector is placed in the resection cavity at surgery — requires a not-yet-completed resection.
trials.postop_timing: Not applicable — vector had to be placed in the resection cavity at the original surgery.
trials.sponsor: University of California San Francisco (with CIRM, Denovo Biopharma, Anova)
trials.us_sites: CA (UCSF, USC, UC San Diego), FL (University of Miami), NY (Northwell).
trials.timing: Vector placed in the cavity at resection + IV within 8 hours — must enrol before the tumour resection.
trials.why_this_fit: The vector must be placed into the resection bed at surgery. That surgery is already done here, so enrolment would have needed to happen before the initial operation. Also note the predecessor agent failed its randomised phase 3.
trials.key_inclusion: Newly diagnosed adult-type diffuse glioma; no prior surgery / radiation / chemotherapy | IDH1 and MGMT testing required | Candidate for ≥80% resection of enhancing tumour; tumour ≤5 cm | Age 18–75; KPS ≥70; platelets ≥60k, Hb ≥10, ANC ≥1500
trials.key_exclusion: IDH-mutant 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma | Multifocal or leptomeningeal disease | Bleeding diathesis / uninterruptible anticoagulation | HIV / hepatitis B / hepatitis C; flucytosine allergy; prior Gliadel wafer
trials.primary_endpoint: Dose-limiting toxicities; treatment-emergent adverse events; phase 2a median PFS by MGMT status.
trials.secondary_endpoints: Recommended phase 2 dose; objective response rate; 6-month PFS; median PFS; overall survival.
trials.outcomes_so_far: The predecessor (Toca 511 + Toca FC) failed its randomised phase 3 in recurrent high-grade glioma — no overall-survival benefit vs standard of care. DB107 is a reformulated newly-diagnosed attempt; efficacy is unproven.
trials.evidence_note: No DB107 results yet. The predecessor (Toca 511 + Toca FC) FAILED its randomised phase 3 (“Toca 5”) in recurrent high-grade glioma — no overall-survival benefit.
trials.flags: Vector delivered at the resection — not compatible with a resection already completed. | Predecessor agent was negative in randomised phase 3.

trials.name: Adenoviral HSV-tk gene therapy + valacyclovir + chemoradiation
trials.evidence_label: Earlier controlled studies showed a survival signal
trials.biomarker_needed: Newly diagnosed anaplastic astrocytoma or GBM (biopsy-proven); IDH / MGMT / EGFR not specified
trials.tissue_requirement: Vector is injected into the resection bed during surgery — requires a not-yet-completed resection.
trials.postop_timing: Not applicable — vector had to be injected into the resection bed during the original surgery.
trials.us_sites: TX — Houston Methodist Neurological Institute, Houston.
trials.timing: Vector injected during surgery; radiation starts within 9 days — enrol before the resection.
trials.why_this_fit: The vector is injected during the tumour surgery and radiation must start within 9 days — enrolment must happen before the initial resection. Single site.
trials.key_inclusion: Newly diagnosed anaplastic astrocytoma or GBM (biopsy-proven) | ECOG 0–1; life expectancy ≥12 weeks | Creatinine <1.5, platelets >100k, ANC >1500, Hb >10 | No multifocal disease >2 cm from the target; no brainstem involvement
trials.key_exclusion: Prior immunotherapy / gene therapy within 3 months; any chemo / radiation / investigational drug within 3 weeks | Cirrhosis or active hepatitis; valacyclovir allergy | HIV or immunocompromise | Leptomeningeal disease with diffuse spinal spread
trials.outcomes_so_far: The same agent (aglatimagene besadenovec + valacyclovir) added to standard chemoradiation showed a survival signal and acceptable safety in earlier controlled newly-diagnosed high-grade glioma studies (Chiocca phase 2; Wheeler/Aggarwal, Neuro-Oncology 2016).
trials.evidence_note: The same agent (aglatimagene besadenovec + valacyclovir) added to standard chemoradiation showed a survival signal and acceptable safety in earlier controlled newly-diagnosed high-grade-glioma studies.
trials.flags: Vector delivered during surgery — not compatible with a resection already completed. | Single site.

trials.name: EF-41 / KEYNOTE-D58 — Optune (TTFields) + temozolomide + pembrolizumab
trials.biomarker_needed: Newly diagnosed GBM (WHO 2021); no IDH / MGMT / EGFR requirement
trials.tissue_requirement: Standard archival tissue — no special banking needed; note US sites are not recruiting regardless.
trials.postop_timing: Only reachable after finishing standard chemoradiation and starting maintenance — many months out. Also not recruiting at US sites regardless.
trials.us_sites: US sites listed but NOT recruiting (Mayo, USC, Hoag, Stanford, UCSF, Georgetown, UF, Moffitt, Northwestern, Duke, MD Anderson and others). Recruiting sites are outside the US.
trials.timing: After completing standard chemoradiation (56–64 Gy + concurrent temozolomide), at the start of maintenance.
trials.why_this_fit: Every listed US site is “active, not recruiting” — US enrolment appears effectively closed, with recruiting sites in Canada, Japan and Europe. Track in case a US site reopens. Standard-of-care TTFields is available outside any trial.
trials.key_inclusion: Age ≥18; newly diagnosed GBM, recovered from debulking surgery (any extent; no Gliadel) | Completed standard chemoradiation | ECOG 0–1; dexamethasone ≤2 mg for 7 days
trials.key_exclusion: Prior PD-1 / PD-L1 / CTLA-4 / OX40 / CD137 therapy | Steroid >2 mg for mass effect | Systemic anti-cancer therapy within 4 weeks; pneumonitis history | Early progression after chemoradiation; infratentorial or leptomeningeal disease
trials.outcomes_so_far: No results yet. Rationale builds on the positive TTFields EF-14 trial (adds ~4.9 months median OS to standard care); the added value of a checkpoint inhibitor in newly diagnosed GBM is unproven.
trials.evidence_note: EF-41 has not reported. It builds on the positive TTFields EF-14 trial (adds ~4.9 months median OS); the added value of pembrolizumab in newly diagnosed GBM is unproven and checkpoint monotherapy was negative here.
trials.flags: US sites are not recruiting — not an enrolment option for a US patient right now.
